slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.brief: de Broglie wavelength comparison of electron and proton at same KE, or accelerated through same potential

stem: An electron of mass $m_e$ and a proton of mass $m_p$ are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelength of the electron to that of the proton, $\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p}$, is:

verdicts.working: Accelerated through same V with same charge magnitude e: kinetic energy qV equal, momentum p = sqrt(2mqV). de Broglie λ = h/p ∝ 1/sqrt(m). Thus λ_e/λ_p = sqrt(m_p/m_e) ≈ 42.85.

working:
When a particle of charge $q$ is accelerated from rest through a potential difference $V$, the kinetic energy gained is:
$$K = qV$$
Both the electron and the proton carry the same magnitude of electric charge, $|q| = e$, so both acquire the same kinetic energy:
$$K_e = K_p = eV$$
The de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ associated with a particle of mass $m$ and kinetic energy $K$ is:
$$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$$
Since $h$, $e$, and $V$ are identical for both particles:
$$\lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$$
Therefore, the ratio of their wavelengths is:
$$\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m_p}{m_e}}$$

Independent check: Accelerated through same V with same charge magnitude e: kinetic energy qV equal, momentum p = sqrt(2mqV). de Broglie λ = h/p ∝ 1/sqrt(m). Thus λ_e/λ_p = sqrt(m_p/m_e) ≈ 42.85.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option B is obtained by inverting the ratio (calculating $\lambda_p/\lambda_e$) or mistakenly assuming $\lambda \propto \sqrt{m}$.
Option C is obtained by forgetting the square root in the relation between momentum and kinetic energy ($p \propto m$ instead of $p = \sqrt{2mK}$).
Option D is obtained by both forgetting the square root and inverting the proportionality (assuming $\lambda \propto m$).
